name: Qatar
headline: Qatar: +1.8% growth in 2025, 0.6% inflation, debt 43% of GDP
sections: Qatar is a $216 billion economy (2025), the world's 57th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +1.8% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $129K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 7.9% of GDP (2025).
Consumer prices rose 0.6% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 5.0% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 0.1% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 0.6% (2025).
Gross government debt is 43% of GDP (2025), a moderate level that has fallen from 73% in 2020. The general government balance is −1.0% of GDP (2025).
The current account balance is +16.4% of GDP (2025), a large surplus. Trade equals 100% of GDP (2022), a highly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 1.4% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 36% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 82.5 years (2024). Population: 3.2 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
